questions.q: A 35-year-old man presents with a painless, indurated ulcer on the glans penis for 3 weeks. The base is clean and the edges are rolled. Non-tender inguinal lymphadenopathy is present. VDRL titre is 1:32. What is the drug of choice?
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM single dose
questions.exp: The presentation is classic primary syphilis (Hunterian chancre). Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM single dose is the drug of choice for primary and secondary syphilis per WHO/CDC guidelines.

questions.q: A 28-year-old farmer presents with a 6-month history of warty, verrucous plaques on the dorsum of the right foot. Black dots are visible within the plaques. KOH mount shows brown, thick-walled sclerotic cells dividing by binary fission. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Chromoblastomycosis presents with verrucous plaques on lower limbs in agricultural workers. KOH mount shows pathognomonic muriform (sclerotic/Medlar) bodies — brown, thick-walled cells with cross-wall septation.

questions.q: A 22-year-old presents with grouped tense vesicles on an erythematous base over the right T5 dermatome associated with severe burning pain. Where does varicella-zoster virus establish latency to cause this condition?
questions.exp: Varicella-zoster virus (VZV) establishes latency in the dorsal root ganglia (sensory ganglia) after primary varicella. Reactivation causes herpes zoster along the affected dermatome.

questions.q: A leprosy patient on MDT develops sudden erythema, warmth, and tenderness of pre-existing skin lesions along with new lesions, fever, and acute nerve function impairment. Slit-skin smear BI is 1+. Which type of lepra reaction is this?
questions.exp: Type 1 (reversal) reaction occurs in borderline leprosy (BT, BB, BL) due to a sudden increase in CMI. It features acute inflammation of existing lesions, new lesions, and acute neuritis. Steroids are the mainstay of treatment.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with tense bullae on normal and erythematous skin predominantly in flexural areas. DIF shows linear IgG and C3 at the DEJ. Which antigen is targeted?
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid: IgG autoantibodies target BP180 (collagen XVII, hemidesmosomal protein) and BP230. DIF shows linear IgG and C3 at the BMZ (subepidermal). It is the most common autoimmune blistering disease in the elderly.

questions.q: A 60-year-old man has a pearly, rolled-edge nodule with telangiectasias on the inner canthus of the left eye, present for 2 years. Dermatoscopy shows arborizing vessels and blue-grey globules. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Nodular basal cell carcinoma classically presents as a pearly papule/nodule with rolled edges, telangiectasias, and central ulceration. Dermatoscopy shows arborizing (tree-like) vessels and blue-grey globules. Inner canthus is a high-risk site.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman with SLE develops photosensitive annular erythematous scaly lesions on the trunk and arms. Anti-Ro/SSA antibodies are strongly positive. Which subtype of cutaneous lupus does this represent?
questions.exp: SCLE presents with photosensitive annular or papulosquamous lesions, strongly associated with anti-Ro/SSA antibodies. It can be drug-induced (hydrochlorothiazide, calcium channel blockers, anti-TNF agents). It heals without scarring.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man presents with thickened skin of the trunk and proximal extremities, Raynaud's phenomenon, and dysphagia. Anti-Scl-70 antibodies are positive. What is the leading cause of death in this condition?
questions.exp: In diffuse cutaneous SSc with anti-Scl-70 (anti-topoisomerase I), pulmonary fibrosis/ILD is the major cause of mortality. Anti-centromere antibodies are associated with limited SSc and pulmonary arterial hypertension.

questions.q: A 4-year-old child presents with honey-colored crusted lesions around the nose and mouth. The causative organism is Streptococcus pyogenes. Which systemic complication is specifically associated with cutaneous (not pharyngeal) streptococcal infection?
questions.exp: Post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis can follow skin infections with nephritogenic strains of Group A Streptococcus. Unlike pharyngitis, skin streptococcal infections do NOT cause rheumatic fever — only throat infections do.

questions.q: A 25-year-old HIV-positive man with CD4 count of 80 cells/μL presents with multiple painless, umbilicated papules on the face and trunk. What is the causative agent of this opportunistic skin infection?
questions.exp: Molluscum contagiosum (caused by a poxvirus, MCV-1 and MCV-2) causes umbilicated papules. In HIV/AIDS with CD4 <200, lesions are extensive on the face and represent a marker of severe immunosuppression. Antiretroviral therapy leads to resolution.

questions.q: A patient with 3 hypopigmented anesthetic skin lesions is classified as paucibacillary leprosy by WHO. Which is the correct WHO MDT regimen for this patient?
opts: Rifampicin 600 mg monthly + Dapsone 100 mg daily for 6 months
Rifampicin 600 mg monthly + Clofazimine 300 mg monthly + Dapsone 100 mg daily for 12 months
Rifampicin 600 mg monthly + Dapsone 100 mg daily for 12 months
Dapsone 100 mg daily monotherapy for 2 years
questions.exp: WHO PB-MDT: Rifampicin 600 mg once monthly (supervised) + Dapsone 100 mg daily for 6 months. MB-MDT adds Clofazimine (300 mg monthly + 50 mg daily) for 12 months.

questions.q: A 50-year-old woman has flaccid blisters on skin and oral mucosa. Blisters rupture easily, leaving raw erosions. Nikolsky sign is positive. DIF shows intercellular IgG in a 'chicken-wire' pattern. What is the target antigen?
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris: IgG autoantibodies against desmoglein 3 (predominant on mucosae) and desmoglein 1 (predominant on skin). DIF shows intercellular IgG. Loss of desmoglein 3 causes suprabasal acantholysis.

questions.q: A 22-year-old presents with soft, pedunculated, cauliflower-like papules in the anogenital region caused by HPV 6 and 11. For large, extensive condylomata acuminata, which treatment offers the best immediate clearance?
questions.exp: For large, extensive condylomata acuminata, surgical excision or electrosurgery provides the most rapid and complete clearance. Patient-applied therapies (imiquimod, podophyllin) are for smaller, limited lesions. TCA is provider-applied but better for small warts.

questions.q: A 35-year-old man has well-demarcated silvery scaly plaques on elbows and knees. Biopsy shows parakeratosis, acanthosis, elongated rete ridges, and neutrophil collections within the parakeratotic stratum corneum. What are these neutrophil collections called?
questions.exp: Munro microabscesses — collections of neutrophils in the parakeratotic stratum corneum — are pathognomonic of psoriasis. Pautrier microabscesses (atypical lymphocytes in epidermis) are seen in mycosis fungoides.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman has a maculopapular rash on palms and soles, condylomata lata in the groin, mucous patches in the mouth, and painless generalized lymphadenopathy. VDRL is 1:128. What stage of syphilis is this?
questions.exp: Secondary syphilis occurs 4–10 weeks after the primary chancre. Features include rash (including palms and soles), condylomata lata, mucous patches, generalized lymphadenopathy, and systemic symptoms. VDRL is strongly reactive.

questions.q: A 19-year-old started on oral isotretinoin for severe nodulocystic acne. Which of the following adverse effects is NOT associated with isotretinoin?
questions.exp: Gynaecomastia is NOT a known side effect of isotretinoin. Side effects include cheilitis (most common), xerosis, hypertriglyceridaemia, transaminase elevation, pseudotumor cerebri (potentiated by concomitant tetracyclines), and teratogenicity.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman is undergoing patch testing for suspected allergic contact dermatitis. According to ICDRG recommendations, where should patch tests be applied?
questions.exp: ICDRG (International Contact Dermatitis Research Group) recommends applying patch tests on the upper back (inter-scapular region). The site provides reproducible results and adequate skin area for multiple allergen application.

questions.q: A 30-year-old with chronic flexural eczema and personal history of asthma has markedly elevated serum IgE. Which cytokine axis primarily drives atopic dermatitis and is targeted by dupilumab?
questions.exp: Atopic dermatitis is driven predominantly by Th2 cytokines: IL-4 (IgE class switching, Th2 differentiation) and IL-13 (skin barrier disruption, fibrosis). Dupilumab blocks IL-4Rα, inhibiting signalling of both IL-4 and IL-13.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man has violaceous, flat-topped, polygonal pruritic papules on the wrists and buccal mucosa showing a lacy white pattern. Biopsy shows band-like lymphocytic infiltrate, saw-tooth rete ridges, and Civatte bodies. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Lichen planus: the 6 Ps (Pruritic, Planar, Polygonal, Purple Papules, and Plaques). Wickham's striae appear as a lacy white pattern on mucosa. Civatte bodies are apoptotic keratinocytes at the DEJ. T-cell mediated autoimmune condition.

questions.q: A 26-year-old woman develops target lesions on palms and soles, erosions of the buccal mucosa, and bilateral conjunctival involvement 2 weeks after starting co-trimoxazole. What is the correct diagnosis?
questions.exp: SJS involves mucosal erosions in ≥2 sites and <10% BSA epidermal detachment. TEN has >30% BSA detachment. Common culprits: sulfonamides (co-trimoxazole), allopurinol, anticonvulsants, NSAIDs. Treatment: stop drug, supportive care, IVIG/cyclosporine.

questions.q: A 40-year-old man with sarcoidosis develops bilateral tender erythematous nodules on the anterior shins. Biopsy shows septal panniculitis without vasculitis. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Erythema nodosum is the most common panniculitis — septal type, without vasculitis. It presents on anterior shins. Causes include sarcoidosis, TB, streptococcal infections, IBD, drugs (OCP). Erythema induratum is a lobular panniculitis associated with TB.

questions.q: A 10-year-old child has pruritic vesicles on an erythematous base simultaneously showing macules, papules, vesicles, and crusts on the scalp, face, and trunk. This 'dew drop on rose petal' appearance is characteristic of which viral infection?
questions.exp: Varicella (chickenpox) caused by VZV presents with pleomorphic lesions in all stages simultaneously ('dew drop on rose petal'). Lesions are centripetal (more on trunk than extremities). Tzanck smear shows multinucleated giant cells.

questions.q: During Mohs micrographic surgery, horizontal frozen sections are cut and examined. What percentage of the tumor surgical margin does this technique allow to be examined, compared to conventional vertical bread-loaf sectioning?
questions.exp: Mohs surgery examines nearly 100% of the surgical margin using horizontal cryosections, enabling precise margin control and maximum tissue conservation. Conventional vertical (bread-loaf) sectioning samples only ~0.1% of the margin, hence the superior cure rates with Mohs.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman has depigmented macules on the dorsal hands and perioral area that enhance on Wood's lamp examination. Melanocytes are absent on skin biopsy. For widespread, stable vitiligo involving >30% BSA, what is the treatment of choice?
questions.exp: Narrow-band UVB (311 nm) phototherapy is the treatment of choice for widespread stable vitiligo. It has replaced oral PUVA due to better safety profile. Topical steroids are used for localized disease. JAK inhibitors (ruxolitinib cream) are newer options.

questions.q: A 35-year-old man has nodular infiltrated plaques on the face, madarosis, pendulous ear lobes, and nasal voice. Slit-skin smear BI is 5+. Histology shows 'Virchow cells' (foamy macrophages laden with bacilli). Which is the correct diagnosis?
questions.exp: Lepromatous leprosy (LL) — polar type with maximal bacterial load. Features: symmetric lesions, leonine facies, madarosis, pendulous earlobes, BI 5–6+, Virchow cells on histology, lepromin (Mitsuda) test negative. Treated with MB-MDT for 12 months.

questions.q: A 48-year-old woman has recurrent, non-pruritic, non-pitting swelling of the lower lip lasting 1–2 days. Her son has similar episodes. Serum C1 esterase inhibitor is low. What mediator primarily drives the angioedema attacks?
questions.exp: Hereditary angioedema (HAE) due to C1-INH deficiency leads to uncontrolled complement activation and excess bradykinin production via the kallikrein-kinin system. Bradykinin (acting on B2 receptors) causes vasodilation and vascular leak. It is non-histaminergic and antihistamines are ineffective.

questions.q: A 20-year-old man has multiple soft pedunculated skin-colored tumors (neurofibromas), more than 6 café-au-lait macules each >1.5 cm, and axillary freckling (Crowe's sign). Which gene is mutated in this autosomal dominant condition?
questions.exp: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (von Recklinghausen disease) is caused by mutations in the NF1 gene on chromosome 17q11.2, encoding neurofibromin — a RAS-GTPase activating protein (tumor suppressor). Autosomal dominant, high penetrance.

questions.q: A 38-year-old woman with SLE has malar erythema, discoid lesions with scarring alopecia, and oral ulcers. ANA 1:320, anti-dsDNA and anti-Sm positive. DIF of non-sun-exposed normal skin shows granular IgG deposits at the DEJ. What is this phenomenon called?
questions.exp: Lupus band test (LBT): DIF of non-sun-exposed normal skin showing granular deposits of IgG, IgM, IgA, and C3 at the DEJ. Positive in ~80% of systemic lupus. Negative in drug-induced lupus and DLE. A positive LBT on normal skin is highly specific for SLE.

questions.q: A 32-year-old male patient presents with recurrent oral ulcers, genital ulcers, and uveitis for 2 years. The pathergy test (intradermal saline injection causing a pustule >2 mm at 48 hours) is positive. HLA-B51 is detected. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Behçet's disease: recurrent oral ulcers + ≥2 of (recurrent genital ulcers, uveitis/retinal vasculitis, skin lesions such as pseudofolliculitis/erythema nodosum, positive pathergy test). Strongly associated with HLA-B51. Common in the 'Silk Road' countries.

questions.q: A 65-year-old woman on long-term hydroxyurea therapy for myeloproliferative disorder presents with painful, hyperpigmented macules, nail changes (longitudinal melanonychia), and lower limb ulcers. Which dermatological complication of hydroxyurea is responsible for the ulcers?
questions.exp: Hydroxyurea causes characteristic dermatomucosal toxicity including leg ulcers (particularly on medial malleoli), dermatomyositis-like eruption, longitudinal melanonychia, and acral hyperpigmentation. Ulcers are due to impaired wound healing and are an indication to stop the drug.
